title: Vuln triage rotation + secrets handoff — 2026-03-25
content:
Meeting: Security engineering sync — weekly (focused on vuln triage rota, secrets incidents, and quick threat-model check)
Date: 2026-03-25 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom / #sec-eng Slack thread
Attendees: Ava Martinez (chair), Samir Patel, Jia Chen, Liam O'Rourke, Maya Singh, Victor Alvarez, + FYI: Ops oncall (Noah)

Summary (TL;DR):
- Triage rotation update: new on-call rotation schedule pushed; two handoff items carried over (ENGSEC-4125, SEC-2183).
- Secrets: one medium finding (expired-but-leaked deploy key) contained; full rotation and audit required for the affected service.
- Threat modeling: quick pass on the new shared-embeddings feature — identified 3 attack surface concerns (exfil via batch cache, permission escalation through model routing, inference poisoning risk).
- Action items assigned with owners and timelines.

Notes / Discussion:
1) Triage rotation and coverage
- New rotation starts Mon 2026-03-29. Samir to be primary for weeks 1–2, Jia backup.
- Rationale: even distribution given upcoming PTO and Dedicated launch spikes.
- Reminder: triage doc (confluence:redwood-security/vuln-playbook) updated yesterday with escalation matrix and SLAs. Check the "urgent" channel for incidents >P2.

2) Vulnerability triage items (current backlog highlights)
- ENGSEC-4125: service-key found in archived repo (platform/service-auth). Severity: Medium (token scope limited to deploy-read). Owner: Samir. Notes: key was expired per secret-manager metadata but still present in history; risk is lower but rotate to be safe. Action: rotate and invalidate in secret-manager by 2026-03-27; new key to follow rotation policy M-3. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2891
- SEC-2183: dependency vuln in third-party transformer wrapper (CVE placeholder: CVE-2026-xxxxx). Severity: High. Owner: Jia. Notes: upgrade path requires small API changes; compatibility tests failing on older models. Action: Jia to open a compatibility-fix PR and coordinate with serving-runtime team; target remediation 2026-04-02.
- New: internal scanner flagged 12 low findings across infra IaC templates — mostly unused ports and stale firewall rules. Owner: Liam. Action: Liam to triage and close low findings by 2026-04-08 or re-categorize if they become exploitable.

3) Secrets posture update
- Incident recap: 2026-03-23, automated commit-hook flagged a deploy key embedded in an archived branch. Quick containment: key invalidated, alert triggered, PR to remove history created.
- Root cause: developer used older local backup during feature handoff; repo-clean wasn’t run.
- Short-term mitigation: enforce repository pre-merge check for secrets with exit-on-positive; expand commit-hook to scan archived branches and refs (Maya to lead). Target: 2026-04-02.
- Long-term: plan to integrate secret-rotation cron for service accounts tied to repo commits (proposal in linked_artifacts).
- Questions unresolved: do we want a mandatory 90-day auto-rotation for all CI/CD service tokens? Cost/complexity analysis needed.

4) Threat modeling — Shared embeddings (quick pass)
- Context: product wants a shared embeddings cache to reduce inference cost for repeated queries across customers.
- Surface concerns identified this meeting:
  * Cache poisoning: attacker could try to insert crafted inputs to influence cached vectors leading to misranked results. Mitigations: input validation, LRU with TTL, model-output sanity checks (owner: Victor, due 2026-04-09).
  * Cross-tenant leakage: risk that embeddings tied to one customer become visible to another through a misrouted cache key. Mitigations: strong tenant scoping in keys, kms-per-tenant or per-region namespace, test harness for tenant isolation (owner: Maya + infra, due 2026-04-16).
  * Escalation via model routing: if routing policy falls back to lower-tier model, adversary could craft workload that spikes fallback and force degraded responses. Mitigations: rate limits per-tenant, anomaly detection on model fallback rates (owner: Jia, prototype by 2026-04-06).
- Follow-up: schedule a full threat-model workshop (2h) after feature spec lands. Aim: 2026-04-12. Invite: product-hosted-api, serving-runtime, infra security.

5) Playbook / runbook items discussed
- Update triage playbook: add steps for archived-branch secrets and a checklist for rotation post-discovery (Ava to edit).
- Add a "who to call" list for P1/P0 oncall escalation; include PagerDuty, Eng manager backups. (Liam)
- Documenting the shared-embeddings threat assumptions in Confluence (Victor).

Action items (owner — due):
- Samir — rotate/invalidate discovered deploy key (ENGSEC-4125) and close ticket — 2026-03-27.
- Jia — open vuln-fix PR for transformer wrapper (SEC-2183); run two-night compatibility tests — 2026-04-02.
- Maya — expand commit-hook to scan archived refs; propose rollout plan — 2026-04-02.
- Liam — triage IaC low findings and update firewall housekeeping doc — 2026-04-08.
- Victor — write shared-embeddings threat assumptions and mitigation stub in Confluence — 2026-04-09.
- Ava — update vuln triage playbook with archived-branch flow and rotation checklist — 2026-03-30.
- Jia + Infra — prototype fallback-anomaly detector (proof-of-concept) — 2026-04-06.

Open questions / risks:
- Auto-rotation policy: scoped (CI/CD tokens only?) vs broad (all service principals). Need cost/ops estimate. (Product + infra input needed)
- Can we safely TTL cached embeddings without measurable SLA impact? Need perf bench (SRE/serving-runtime).
- Dependency fix (SEC-2183) may require temporary canary on Dedicated nodes to validate latency. Coordinate with Dedicated team.

Notes to record in ticket system:
- ENGSEC-4125: tag with "secrets-leak", "archived-branch" and link PR removing history.
- SEC-2183: mark as "needs-canary" if tests require Dedicated nodes.

Misc / FYI
- Next sync: 2026-04-01 (same time). Proposed focus: post-mortem on secrets incident + canary plan for dependency patching.
- Quick wins: enable archived-ref scanning earlier in the week to reduce recurrence.

Raw scratchpad entries (copied from chat during meeting):
- "Samir: we should treat archived branches like active refs for scanning"
- "Maya: maybe a PR bot that auto-opens rotation PRs for service accounts"
- "Victor: add per-tenant namespace to cache keys, flag if same-key used across tenants"

References and links repeated for convenience:
- Vulnerability playbook: confluence:redwood-security/vuln-playbook
- ENGSEC-4125 (Linear): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENGSEC-4125/rotate-service-keys-found-in-repo
- SEC-2183 (Jira): jira:SEC-2183
- PR removing key history: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2891

End of notes.

Document history: first draft for distribution to sec-eng list; will archive to Confluence after approvals and after playbook edits.
